rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoid what God dislikes, especially anything that harms His Messenger, and speak purposefully toward the truth.
rows.anchor: في ارتكاب ما يكرهه فضلا عما يؤذي رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl sadīd is speech directed to truth; this also prohibits its opposite, as illustrated by an unintentional report from Zaynab.
rows.anchor: قاصدا إلى الحق من سد يسد سدادا، والمراد النهي عن ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may enable good deeds or make them righteous by accepting and rewarding them; upright speech and action expiate sins.
rows.anchor: يوفقكم للأعمال الصالحة، أو يصلحها بالقبول والإثابة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying God and His Messenger in commands and prohibitions brings great success in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: يعيش في الدنيا حميدا وفي الآخرة سعيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust is named amāna because its performance is obligatory; this reinforces the preceding promise by magnifying obedience.
rows.anchor: تقرير للوعد السابق بتعظيم الطاعة، وسماها أمانة من حيث إنها واجبة الأداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer to immense celestial bodies is a hypothetical emphasizing the trust's gravity: if conscious, they would refuse and fear it, while frail humans carried it.
rows.anchor: لو عرضت على هذه الأجرام العظام وكانت ذات شعور وإدراك لأبين أن يحملنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safeguarding the trust and fulfilling its rights brings good in both abodes; people are generally unjust for failing it and ignorant of its consequences.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يف بها ولم يراع حقها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the trust as obedience, natural or voluntary; its offer is a request to the willing and divine willing of acts from others, while carrying can mean betrayal or failure.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد ب { الأمانة } الطاعة التى تعم الطبيعية والاختيارية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says God gave the celestial bodies understanding and offered a duty with reward and punishment; they declined, while Adam accepted and thereby wronged himself and misjudged its burden.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه تعالى لما خلق هذه الأجرام خلق فيها فهما وقال لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust may instead mean reason or religious obligation; the offer tested readiness, celestial refusal was natural incapacity, and human acceptance reflects capacity while anger and appetite make people unjust and ignorant.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد ب { الأمانة } العقل أو التكليف، وبعرضها عليهن اعتبارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, reason governs anger and appetite, while obligation aims chiefly to moderate and restrain them.
rows.anchor: من فوائد العقل أن يكون مهيمنا على القوتين حافظا لهما عن التعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā here means adhering to God's obedience.
rows.anchor: بلزوم طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good through worldly obedience brings a good afterlife reward; another reading makes the good health and well-being in this world, with the phrase locating it.
rows.anchor: أي للذين أحسنوا بالطاعات في الدنيا مثوبة حسنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's breadth permits anyone unable to practice goodness in their homeland to migrate to somewhere they can.
rows.anchor: فمن تعسر عليه التوفر على الإحسان في وطنه فليهاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient endure hardship in obedience, trials, and migration; their reward exceeds what any reckoning can comprehend.
rows.anchor: على مشاق الطاعات من احتمال البلاء ومهاجرة الأوطان لها

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A report says scales are set for prayer, charity, and pilgrimage, but afflicted people receive reward poured on them without measure, until the healthy wish for their trial.
rows.anchor: ولا ينصب لأهل البلاء بل يصب عليهم الأجر صبا حتى يتمنى أهل العافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and evil are unequal in recompense and outcome; the second lā reinforces the negation.
rows.anchor: في الجزاء وحسن العاقبة و { لا } الثانية مزيدة لتأكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Answer an encountered evil with better goodness, or the best possible good response; presenting it as an answer to how to act intensifies the command and substitutes better for goodness.
rows.anchor: ادفع السيئة حيث اعترضتك بالتي هي أحسن منها وهي الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This response may transform a hostile enemy into a compassionate close friend.
rows.anchor: صار عدوك المشاق مثل الولي الشفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disposition means answering injury with goodness; patience restrains revenge, so only the patient attain it.
rows.anchor: وما يلقى هذه السجية وهي مقابلته الإساءة بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great share means abundant good and perfection of the soul; another view identifies it as Paradise.
rows.anchor: من الخير وكمال النفس وقيل الحظ الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse on the conjecturers means lying advocates of contradictory claims; the expression began as a prayer for death and came to function like a curse.
rows.anchor: الكذابون من أصحاب القول المختلف، وأصله الدعاء بالقتل أجري مجرى اللعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are submerged in ignorance and heedless of what they were commanded.
rows.anchor: في جهل يغمرهم. { سهون } غافلون عما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask when the recompense will occur; a variant reads iyāna with kasra.
rows.anchor: أي فيقولون متى يوم الجزاء أي وقوعه، وقرىء { إيان } بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is when they are burned, either answering their question or in apposition; yawm is opened because it is annexed to an indeclinable word, with a nominative variant.
rows.anchor: يحرقون جواب للسؤال أي يقع { يوم هم على النار يفتنون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to taste their trial is spoken to them; the following phrase identifies the punishment they had demanded hastily.
rows.anchor: أي مقولا لهم هذا القول. { هذا الذى كنتم به تستعجلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing accept with satisfaction what their Lord gives them; all of it is good and received willingly, explaining their entitlement through prior good works.
rows.anchor: قابلين لما أعطاهم راضين به، ومعناه أن كل ما آتاهم حسن مرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise points to unbelievers' rejection and calling the Messenger a magician or madman; the following clause explains the comparison.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر مثل ذلك، والإشارة إلى تكذيبهم الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase after the negative mā cannot govern what precedes it, so the following clause cannot be made the object of the verb.
rows.anchor: لأن ما بعد { ما } النافية لا يعمل فيما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question pictures earlier and later peoples as if they had passed the same accusation to each other; the author says shared tyranny, not actual cross-generational counsel, explains it.
rows.anchor: كأن الأولين والآخرين منهم أوصى بعضهم بعضا بهذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects actual counsel because those generations were far apart in time; their shared tyranny prompted the accusation.
rows.anchor: الجامع لهم على هذا القول مشاركتهم في الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After repeated calls meet only stubborn refusal, the Messenger should stop disputing; he is not blameworthy after doing his utmost to convey the message.
rows.anchor: فأعرض عن مجادلتهم بعدما كررت عليهم الدعوة فأبوا إلا الإصرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created heaven elevated in place and rank as the source of decrees and rulings and the abode of angels; another reading makes al-samāʾ nominative as a subject.
rows.anchor: خلقها مرفوعة محلا ومرتبة، فإنها منشأ أقضيته ومتنزل أحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance may mean justice, giving each deserving recipient their due and every rights-holder their right, thereby ordering the world.
rows.anchor: العدل بأن وفر على كل مستعد مستحقه، ووفى كل ذي حق حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying is cited that justice established the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام " بالعدل قامت السموات والأرض "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the balance is an instrument such as scales or a measure that reveals amounts and equitable rights on earth.
rows.anchor: أو ما يعرف به مقادير الأشياء من ميزان ومكيال ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not transgress the balance or exceed fairness; a variant reads lā taṭghaw as quoted speech.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعتدوا ولا تجاوزوا الانصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Set weight fairly and do not diminish the balance, since fairness is its purpose; repetition intensifies the exhortation and several vocalizations are reported.
rows.anchor: ولا تنقصوه فإن من حقه أن يسوى لأنه المقصود من وضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah can mean the Hour, an event certain to occur, one in which realities become known, or one in which reckoning and recompense occur by figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: أي الساعة أو الحالة التي يحق وقوعها، أو التي تحق فيها الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means what is it and magnifies the event; the explicit noun replaces a pronoun to make its terror more forceful.
rows.anchor: وأصله ما هي أي: أي شيء هي على التعظيم لشأنها والتهويل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can know the event's true nature, for it is beyond anyone's grasp; grammatically mā is subject and adrāka its predicate.
rows.anchor: أي أنك لا تعلم كنهها فإنها أعظم من أن تبلغها دراية أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the calamity that terrifies people and makes bodies split and scatter; its name heightens the severity.
rows.anchor: بالحالة التي تقرع فيها الناس بالإفزاع والأجرام بالانفطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed humanity the path by setting out proofs and sending down signs.
rows.anchor: أي بنصب الدلائل وإنزال الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thankful and ungrateful are two states of the human referent: all are shown the path, then some follow it and some turn away; alternatively they qualify the path figuratively.
rows.anchor: أي { هدينه } في حاليه جميعا أو مقسوما إليهما بعضهم { شكرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥ on ammā omits the response; ungrateful rather than unbelieving preserves the rhyme and signals widespread ingratitude, though culpability lies in deep indulgence.
rows.anchor: محافظة على الفواصل، وإشعارا بأن الإنسان لا يخلو عن كفران غالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Chains lead the unbelievers, fetters bind them, and fire burns them; their warning comes first because it is more beneficial, while framing the discourse with believers is more fitting.
rows.anchor: بها يقادون. { وأغللا } بها يقيدون. { وسعيرا } بها يحرقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr read salāsilā with a final alif for rhyme.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع والكسائي وأبو بكر «سلاسلا» للمناسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṭfīf is shortchanging in measure or weight because what is withheld is slight or trivial.
rows.anchor: التطفيف البخس في الكيل والوزن لأن ما يبخس طفيف أي حقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Medina's people were the worst measurers; after this verse came down, they improved their measuring.
rows.anchor: روي أن أهل المدينة كانوا أخبث الناس كيلا فنزلت فأحسنوه

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A report warns of enemies for broken covenants, poverty for unjust rule, death with immorality, crop failure and famine for short measure, and withheld rain for unpaid alms.
rows.anchor: ولا طففوا الكيل إلا منعوا النبات وأخذوا بالسنين، ولا منعوا الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cheaters take their dues from people in full; ʿalā instead of min marks a due owed by others or oppressive measuring against them.
rows.anchor: أي إذا اكتالوا من الناس حقوقهم يأخذونها وافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they measure or weigh for people, the preposition is omitted and the verb made transitive, as supported by the cited poetry.
rows.anchor: أي إذا كالوا الناس أو وزنوا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the omitted object is their measured amount; treating the separate pronoun as emphasis for the attached pronoun disrupts the contrast of taking and giving and conflicts with Qur'anic spelling.
rows.anchor: ولا يحسن جعل المنفصل تأكيدا للمتصل فإنه يخرج الكلام عن مقابلة ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who believed in resurrection would not dare such offenses; the verse rebukes their behavior, even more so if they were certain.
rows.anchor: فإن من ظن ذلك لم يتجاسر على أمثال هذه القبائح، فكيف بمن تيقنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is great because of its events; the phrase may modify the raising or substitute for the preceding prepositional phrase, supported by a genitive reading.
rows.anchor: عظمه لعظم ما يكون فيه { يوم يقوم الناس } نصب بمبعوثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke, mention of belief, great day, standing before God, and naming Him Lord of the worlds all intensify the warning against cheating.
rows.anchor: مبالغات في المنع عن التطفيف وتعظيم إثمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers fail to believe in resurrection and fail to prostrate at Qur'an recitation, either by humbling themselves or performing recitation prostration.
rows.anchor: لا يخضعون أو { لا يسجدون } لتلاوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited al-ʿAlaq 96:19 and prostrated with the believers while Quraysh clapped overhead, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فسجد بمن معه من المؤمنين وقريش تصفق فوق رؤوسهم فنزلت

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah cites the rebuke of those who heard but did not prostrate as proof that recitation prostration is obligatory.
rows.anchor: واحتج به أبو حنيفة على وجوب السجود فإنه ذم لمن سمعه ولم يسجد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayrah says he prostrated at this passage only after seeing the Messenger prostrate there.
rows.anchor: أنه سجد فيها وقال: والله ما سجدت فيها إلا بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers deny the Qur'an, while God knows the disbelief and hostility concealed in their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي بالقرآن. { والله أعلم بما يوعون } بما يضمرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to tell them of painful punishment is a taunt.
rows.anchor: { فبشرهم بعذاب أليم } استهزاء بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception can be connected or disconnected and means those who repent and believe; their reward is uninterrupted or not held over them as a favor.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أو متصل، والمراد من تاب وآمن منهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises that readers of al-Inshiqāq will be spared receiving their book from behind their backs.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الانشقاق أعاذه الله أن يعطيه كتابه وراء ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful for blessing, disobedient in Kinda's dialect, or miserly in Banū Mālik's dialect.
rows.anchor: لكفور من كند النعمة كنودا، أو لعاص بلغة كندة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human may witness against himself through visible effects of ingratitude, or God may be the witness as a threat.
rows.anchor: يشهد على نفسه لظهور أثره عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khayr means wealth; being intense in love of it means either miserly or strongly attached to it.
rows.anchor: المال من قوله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿthara means resurrection; variants include baḥthara and baḥata.
rows.anchor: بعث. { ما فى القبور } من الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is gathered or sifted from people's breasts is good or evil; they are singled out as its source.
rows.anchor: جمع محصلا في الصحف أو ميز. { ما فى الصدور }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows and requites what people disclose and conceal on Judgment Day; shifting from mā to bihim reflects their different states, and readings omit the initial particle or lām.
rows.anchor: عالم بما أعلنوا وما أسروا فيجازيهم عليه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reading al-ʿĀdiyāt per person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and attended Jamʿ.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة والعاديات أعطى من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamz means breaking and lamz stabbing; both became terms for damaging people's reputations. Their intensive pattern marks habitual behavior.
rows.anchor: الهمز الكسر كالهزم، واللمز الطعن كاللهز فشاعا في الكسر من أعراض الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant with sukūn makes the forms passive, describing someone who entertains people and is laughed at and insulted.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «همزة لمزة» بالسكون على بناء المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion is reported as either al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, both said to have slandered the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ونزولها في الأخنس بن شريق فإنه كان مغيابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description can grammatically substitute for every slanderer or be a censure in the accusative or nominative; Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read with a doubled mīm.
rows.anchor: بدل من كل أو ذم منصوب أو مرفوع، وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He made wealth provision for calamities or accumulated it repeatedly; a variant separates the doubling.
rows.anchor: وجعله عدة للنوازل أو عدة مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man may think wealth left him immortal, be distracted from death by loving it, or develop such long hopes that he lives as if he will not die.
rows.anchor: تركه خالدا في الدنيا فأحبه كما يحب الخلود، أو حب المال أغفله عن الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording hints that true immortality lies in striving for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: بأن المخلد هو السعي للآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic jamʿ evokes massing, assembly, and concentrated strength; here it pictures the raiders breaking into a gathered crowd amid raised dust.
rows.anchor: وبكل ما لهذا اللفظ من دلالات الحشد، والتجمع، ومظنة القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene reaches its peak, leaving the reader to imagine the bewildered scattering, confusion, and surrender following the sudden dawn raid.
rows.anchor: هنا بلغ المشهد ذروته، ثم يترك للتصور أن يذهب كل مذهب فيما يعقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns from the familiar scene to certain unseen events and states the oath's answer: humanity is ungrateful to its Lord and loves wealth intensely.
rows.anchor: وتمضي الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that humanity is ungrateful to its Lord and intensely loves wealth is the answer to the preceding oath.
rows.anchor: وبين هذا المشهد المألوف الواقع، وذاك الغيب الذي سوف يقع يقيناً، يأتي المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across Qur'anic uses, al-insān denotes a morally accountable human tested by good and evil, temptation, vanity, and tyranny, bearing obligations beyond being simply one of humankind.
rows.anchor: في سياق الأهلية لاحتمال تبعات التكليف، والابتلاء بالخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gives al-insān knowledge, articulate expression, and disputation and makes it the bearer of admonition and trust.
rows.anchor: الإنسان في القرآن الكريم، لا الإنس، هو الذي أختص بالعلم

rows.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib connects the word insān with sociability and familiarity with a group; the author accepts this as fitting Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: وللراغب الأصفهاني ملحظ دقيق في اشتقاق لفظ الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-ʿAṣr the word denotes human responsibility for the burdens of obligation, individually and socially.
rows.anchor: في سورة العصر، في سياق ما يحتمل من تبعات التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusr opposes profit, first denoting commercial loss, then deficiency, injustice, weakness, betrayal, or fraud, and religiously deviation from truth.
rows.anchor: والخسر لغة نقيض الربح، استعمل مادياً في التجارة الخاسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusr applies materially to trade and measurement and morally to Joseph's brothers and Cain, but most Qur'anic uses warn of religious error and punishment.
rows.anchor: والغالب لأن يأتي الخسر بالمعنى الديني، في سياق النذير بسوء العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss may encompass self, wealth, family, and deeds and is especially clear at resurrection as loss of both worlds.
rows.anchor: ويؤذن السياق فيها بأن الخسر يتعلق بالنفس والمال والأهل والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include the failed at God's judgment, those who lose themselves and their families at resurrection, and those whose work is nullified by disbelief.
rows.anchor: الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls those who obstruct God's path and disbelieve in the afterlife the greatest losers and describes Satan's party as losers.
rows.anchor: أربع مرات للذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusrān mubīn describes taking Satan as patron and conditional worship that turns away after hardship; the author adds al-Zumar as a parallel.
rows.anchor: فجاء بصيغة خسران ثلاث مرات، موصوفاً فيها بالمبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasār is used of Noah's people, wrongdoers, and disbelievers; takhsīr appears in Hūd, while khusr occurs in al-ʿAṣr and al-Ṭalāq for ruin from error and rebellion.
rows.anchor: وبصيغة الخسار، ثلاث مرات كذلك، في قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survey distinguishes religious loss from material loss while tracing the Qur'anic forms of the root.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستقراء يتيح لنا أن نقول إن الخسر يأتي في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects al-Rāghib's claim that all Qur'anic khusr concerns faith and never property or trade, since some contexts explicitly concern measurement.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاحتياط هو ما فات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects al-Zamakhsharī's trade metaphor in which everyone loses a worldly bargain except the righteous who buy the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فلا نستريح إلى تأويل الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She also declines al-Rāzī's claim that everyone loses by wasting life's capital, even through permissible acts or imperfect worship.
rows.anchor: كما لا نتعلق بما ساقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit exception means believers who act righteously and counsel truth and patience are never in loss.
rows.anchor: وصريح النص في الآية بعد الخسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī conveys being surrounded, immersed, or engulfed by loss.
rows.anchor: من معنى الظرفية، في الغمر والإحاطة والإغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against al-Nīsābūrī, the indefinite form khusr is not simply an intensifier; she reads it as open-ended and unrestricted.
rows.anchor: المبالغات كما ذهب النيسابورى. وإنما التنكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indefiniteness may also convey awe, as al-Rāzī suggests: the loss is so great that only God comprehends it.
rows.anchor: على ما قال الرازي. ووجهه عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īmān opposes disbelief and carries the original sense of security and trust; ṣāliḥāt are religious good works opposed to sins.
rows.anchor: الإيمان نقيض الكفر، وفي دلالته اللغوية الأصلية حس الأمن والأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse makes faith and good works individual duties, and mutual counsel in truth and patience a communal responsibility.
rows.anchor: على الإنسان مسئوليته فرداً بالإيمان وعمل الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an often pairs faith and good works, promising believers safety, good life, reward, forgiveness, provision, succession, affection, and Paradise.
rows.anchor: ويقترن العمل الصالح بالإيمان في القرآن الكريم نحو خمس وسبعين مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good works are attributed to messengers and righteous people and appear in the prayers of Joseph, Abraham, and Solomon.
rows.anchor: ويأتي العمل الصالح مسنداً إلى رسل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links good works with rejecting shirk in al-Kahf and contrasts them with disbelief in al-Rūm.
rows.anchor: وعطف النهي عن الشرك على العمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿtazilites and Ashʿarites disputed whether works are called righteous because they intrinsically embody goodness or because God commanded them.
rows.anchor: كالذي ثار بين المعتزلة والأشعرية من خلاف حول تسمية الأعمال بالصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some argue that coordinating good works with faith proves works are outside faith, since otherwise it repeats the same idea; they reject examples that restate an honorable subset after a general term.
rows.anchor: الوقوف عند عطف عمل الصالحاتعلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their opponents note that the same sūrah coordinates mutual counsel in truth and patience after good works and allow repetition for emphasis, while conceding that repetition is not the default.
rows.anchor: لا نمنع التكرير لأجل التأكيد. ولكن الأصل عدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her survey shows that faith is often followed by good works, signaling that faith should be joined to action rather than making the coordination empty repetition.
rows.anchor: فلا يكون هذا تكريراً للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq is the opposite of falsehood; Arabic uses it for a straight thrust, tightly woven cloth, and a mature camel, then for justice, truth, and fate.
rows.anchor: الحق هنا نقيض الباطل. والعربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root's sense of firmness develops into truth and religious use as a divine name, revelation, and religion.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم شاع استعماله في نقيض الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if righteous works are included in faith, their separate mention is specification after generality, highlighting the value and place of good works.
rows.anchor: فيه تنبيه إلى قيمة عمل الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawāṣī means people counsel one another; its root conveys strong connection, as in a palm frond used for binding and a bequest that conveys an instruction to its recipient.
rows.anchor: والتواصي: أن يوصى بعضهم بعضاً. والأصل اللغوي للمادة يعطي معنى قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses waṣṣā and awṣā for divine instruction and often a testament; tawāṣaw occurs five times, including the question whether earlier peoples conspired to reject messengers.
rows.anchor: أما التواضي فجاء في القرآن خمس مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rights involving wealth and family law carry religious sanctity and Resurrection is named al-Ḥāqqah.
rows.anchor: بما لهذه الحقوق من حرمة دينية تجعلها من حدود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic term includes divinely protected rights in wealth, inheritance, marriage, and divorce.
rows.anchor: ما فرض الله على ذوي المال من حق معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religious weight of ḥaqq gives it awe and solemnity in mutual counsel.
rows.anchor: ويؤكد حرمتها في التواصي بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Balad also links faith and mutual counsel in patience and compassion after freeing a slave or feeding the needy; both Meccan sūrahs state foundational teachings.
rows.anchor: ثم كان من الذين آمنوا وتواصوا بالصبر وتواصوا بالمرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣabr opposes panic; its concrete senses include bitter sap, sour milk, coarse stones, severe war or calamity, cold, restraint, and execution while bound.
rows.anchor: والصبر في العربية نقيض الجزع. ومن استعماله في الحسيات

rows.speaker: الإمام الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains patience as perseverance in obedience; al-Zamakhsharī includes avoiding sins, obeying, and enduring God's tests, with Abū Ḥayyān close.
rows.anchor: وقد فسره الإمام الطبري بالصبر على العمل بطاعة الله

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says patience includes fulfilling duties and avoiding prohibitions, since both doing what is disliked and restraining desire are hard; truth is burdensome and accompanied by trials.
rows.anchor: إن التواصي بالصبر يدخل فيه حمل النفس على مشقة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She accepts these as close interpretations, scarcely different from Muḥammad ʿAbduh's commentary.
rows.anchor: وكلها أقوال متقاربة مقبولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to endure the burdens of conveying his message and facing rejection and verbal or physical harm in about twenty passages.
rows.anchor: من أعباء تبليغ رسالته، ما يلقى من تكذيب وأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are told to seek God's aid through patience and prayer and persevere in battle.
rows.anchor: وأمر الله المؤمنين بأن يستعينوا بالله، وبالصبر والصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is attributed to prophets, resolute messengers, earlier messengers, guiding leaders, and believers rewarded with a good final home.
rows.anchor: وجاء الصبر مسنداً إلى أولي العزم من الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience verses address prophets and believers, apart from warnings to the lost that patience or panic in Hell will not help.
rows.anchor: وآيات الصبر في القرآن الكريم لا تتجه إلى غير هذه الصفوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also depicts idolaters persisting in their idols, error, and disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقريب منها صبر المشركين على آلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers' patience bears on trials, calamities, hardship, warfare, migration after persecution, and steadfastness; God loves and accompanies the patient.
rows.anchor: ومما يتعلق به صبر المؤمنين: الابتلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving patience's object unstated in al-ʿAṣr and al-Balad broadens it to Qur'anic demands including faith, testing, ease, hardship, and battle.
rows.anchor: والسكوت عن ذكر متعلق الصبر الذي يتواصى به الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel in truth and patience is a religious duty to the community, covering obligations, testing, prosperity, hardship, and combat.
rows.anchor: مما يصبر عليه المؤمنين من تكاليف الإيمان، والإبتلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an rejects passive individualism: faith and good deeds alone do not discharge the communal duty; righteous individuals benefit society by avoiding harm to others.
rows.anchor: وموقف القرآن من هذه التبعية، يقطع برفض السلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions whether merely professing the testimony, worshipping, and avoiding wrongdoing can suffice; the passage ends before completing the thought.
rows.anchor: أن الإيمان يكفي فيه النطق بالشهادتين وأداء العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah is Meccan and commonly placed thirty-second in revelation order.
rows.anchor: السورة مكية. والمشهور في ترتيب نزولها أنها الثانية والثلاثون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported occasion is al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who mocked and backbit people, especially the Messenger.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت في "الأخنس بن شريق" كان يلمز الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, who backbit the Prophet privately and attacked him to his face.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في "الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي" كان يغتاب

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says people had long heard that the sūrah was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق في السيرة النبوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific person is uncertain, but the warning applies to every slanderer; al-Ṭabarī considers this correct.
rows.anchor: وأياً من كان الذي نزلت فيه السورة، فالنذير عام لكل همزة لمزة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows a specific occasion and a general warning covering everyone who commits the offense.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون السبب خاصاً والوعيد عاماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl means punishment and anger and often appears in lament; some exegetes interpret it as a valley of Hell filled with pus.
rows.anchor: ويل: كلمة عذاب وسخط. ويكثر استعمالها مع هاء الندبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author counts forty Qur'anic occurrences of wayl, thirteen definite in regret and lament contexts, with examples across many sūrahs.
rows.anchor: نجدها في أربعين موضعاً. منها ثلاث عشرة مرة، معرفة بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other uses of wayl are divine warnings; apart from one definite instance, the word is indefinite as here and warns disbelievers, wrongdoers, short-measurers, inattentive worshippers, and slanderers.
rows.anchor: وباقي الآيات الأربعين، في سياق النذير من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survey conveys wayl's dread without interpreting it as a valley of pus; she suspects that interpretation is an Isrāʾīliyyāt addition.
rows.anchor: دون أن نحتاج فيه إلى تأويل بواد في جهنم يسيل قيحاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humaza appears only here; related forms hammāz and hamazāt occur for slander and satanic prompting.
rows.anchor: بهذه الصيغة في القرآن الكريم إلا هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lumaza as a noun also occurs only here; the verb appears in verses about name-calling and criticizing the Prophet's alms distribution.
rows.anchor: في القرآن كله إلا في آية الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that humaza and lumaza denote habitual behavior but disagree about the distinction between the two terms.
rows.anchor: بين اللغويين والمفسرين، في أن مثل صيغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some see no difference; others assign hamz to disparagement behind someone's back and lamz to explicit mockery, while others reverse the meanings.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يجعل الهمز للتحقير والعيب في الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic usage distinguishes hidden hamz in Satanic whispering and slander from face-to-face lamz in name-calling and criticizing the alms division.
rows.anchor: ونحتكم إلى القرآن الكريم فيجلو لنا الفرق بين اللفظين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic physical usage supports the distinction: lamz is a strike or stab, while hamz evokes a notch or hidden prod.
rows.anchor: فاستعملت اللمز في الضرب والطعن. واستعملت الهمز حسياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects Muḥammad ʿAbduh's view that hamz uses eye, lip, or hand gestures while lamz uses the tongue; she assigns hidden disparagement to hamz and direct insult to lamz.
rows.anchor: فلا نذهب مع الشيخ محمد عبده إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hamaza habitually wounds people behind their backs; a lamaza habitually confronts people with abusive words that belittle them.
rows.anchor: وإنما نطمئن إلى أن الهمزة هو الذي يدأب على تحقير الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read jammaʿa with doubled mīm; the other readers use the undoubled form.
rows.anchor: {جَمَّعَ} بتشديد الميم. والباقون بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers agree on doubled dāl in ʿaddadahu apart from an unsupported light reading; al-Ṭabarī rejects that reading for opposing the regional consensus.
rows.anchor: وهذه قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها، لخلافها قراءة الأمصار

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī interprets the public reading as collecting, preserving, and counting wealth without spending for God's cause or paying its due.
rows.anchor: جمع مالاً وحفظه وأحصى عدده ولم ينفقه في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the doubled reading suggests accumulating wealth from many places over time, unlike the undoubled form.
rows.anchor: إن جمع بالتشديد يفيد أنه جمعه من ههنا وههنا

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī offers storage as provision for calamities, counting, tallying, or a large retinue as meanings of ʿaddadahu.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من العدة وهي الذخيرة لحوادث الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamʿ means bringing together scattered, varied individuals and names a group, mixed people, a gathering, or the act of assembling.
rows.anchor: والجمع في اللغة ضد التفرق، مع ملحظ من التفاوت بين أفراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious usages include congregational prayer and the Day of Gathering, when varied peoples, classes, and beliefs assemble.
rows.anchor: كما سمى اليوم الآخر يوم الجمع، يجمع الناس على اختلاف أجناسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simple verb occurs eighteen times with its root sense of gathering scattered things; the doubled form has no Qur'anic derivative.
rows.anchor: وجاء الفعل ثلاثياً ثماني عشرة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In thirteen instances God gathers people in guidance, reassembles bones, or gathers humanity for Judgment and the Day of Decision.
rows.anchor: منها ثلاث عشرة مرة، الفعل فيها مسند إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples include possessions people gather and the massing of troops and weapons against believers.
rows.anchor: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on joining two sisters is an exception to separation of bloodlines; the survey shows jamʿ evokes massing and mingling.
rows.anchor: ولا يتختلف الملحظ في آية المحارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoarder gathers mixed wealth and counts it repeatedly; wealth becomes an idol breeding possessiveness, tyranny, pride, and contempt, as in al-Maʿārij.
rows.anchor: فملحظ الحشد مع الإختلاط، هو ما يعطيه هذا الاستقراء عن قرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥisāb means counting materially and estimation, planning, or accountability figuratively; religious reckoning is especially associated with God.
rows.anchor: كما تستعمله معنوياً في التقدير والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic commonly uses kasra for counting and fatḥa for estimation; ḥasab also means inherited family distinctions.
rows.anchor: فيغلب كسر السين للحساب بمعنى العد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic tri-form hasiba occurs with the sense of estimation by supposition, as when the Queen of Sheba mistakes the floor for water.
rows.anchor: يؤذن سياقها أنها بمعنى التقدير عن ظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative uses of hasiba often rebuke deluded assumptions about escaping trial, equaling believers, hidden grudges, or purposeless creation.
rows.anchor: ويكثر مجيئه بأسلوب الاستفهام الإنكاري، فيعطيه السياق دلالة ضلال الوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All thirty-one occurrences of the open-fātha present yaḥsabu warn against human misestimation.
rows.anchor: بمجئ الفعل المضارع مفتوح السين في آياته الإحدى والثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the word in al-Humazah means a false assumption that wealth made its owner immortal.
rows.anchor: على التوهم الذي يخطئ حقيقة التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuld means permanent endurance; the Qur'an reserves eternal life for the afterlife and denies worldly immortality for human beings.
rows.anchor: والخلد في العربية البقاء والدوام، استعملته حسياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to monuments built to live forever parallels the hoarder's delusion; wealth blinds him to the world's transience.
rows.anchor: فيضله الوهم ضلالاً بعيداً، ويعيمه عن حقيقة الدنيا الفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes and warns before the threat that the hoarder will be cast into al-Ḥuṭamah.
rows.anchor: مع الردع والزجر بـ: كلا، يأتي هذا النبذ في الحطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh means casting aside something deemed worthless; related words describe an outcast child, foundling, remote grave, emaciated camel, and rabble.
rows.anchor: والنبذ في العربية الطرح لما هو هين وحقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intibādh is withdrawal to a secluded place, as in Mary's story; in war nabdh can mean renouncing a treaty openly.
rows.anchor: والانتباذ التنحي والانسحاب إلى مكان مهجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apart from Mary's withdrawal and treaty renunciation, Qur'anic nabdh means casting away in disdain; emphatic lām and nūn threaten humiliation for the miser who humiliates others.
rows.anchor: وبكل ما في لفظ النبذ من دلالة على الهوان والضياع

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī interprets the threat as casting the offender into the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقد فسرها الإمام "الطبري" بالقذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She prefers the native lexical sense of īṣād as tightly shutting, supported by Qur'anic uses of waṣīd in al-Kahf and muʾṣadah at the end of al-Balad.
rows.anchor: ونؤثر أن نستأنس في فهم الآية، بالحس اللغوي الأصيل للإيصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sealed fire parallels al-Balad's description of fire closed upon its occupants, following a warning against boasting of wealth and thinking no one sees.
rows.anchor: وفي آية البلد من إيصاد النار وإطباقها المباشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closed fire with extended columns warns the slanderer who hoards wealth and imagines it makes him immortal.
rows.anchor: نذيراً كذلك ووعيداً بويل {لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ (1)
